meta.title: Peregrine: Free Open-Source Download Manager for Windows, macOS & Linux
meta.description: Peregrine is a free, open-source download manager and IDM alternative. Up to 32 connections per file, resume that survives crashes, a browser extension, torrents and video. No ads, no tracking.
meta.ogTitle: Peregrine: downloads that don’t start over
meta.ogDescription: A free, open-source download manager. Up to 32 connections per file, crash-proof resume, browser extension, torrents and video. No ads, no tracking.

hero.kicker: Free download manager · Windows · macOS · Linux CLI
hero.title: Downloads that don’t start over.
hero.lead: Peregrine splits every file into up to 32 connections, keeps moving them onto the slowest part, and saves progress to disk every second. A dropped Wi-Fi, a crash or a power cut costs you seconds. Never the file.
hero.facts: GPL-3.0 · no ads · no account · no telemetry

how.label: 01 · Speed
how.title: Every connection works until the last byte.
how.body: Most download managers cut a file into fixed parts. The fast parts finish early and sit idle while one slow part drags the whole download out. Peregrine keeps cutting: when a connection finishes, it takes over half of the slowest part that is left. That is what you just watched above.
stats: connections per file, re-balanced while it runs
between progress saves to a crash-safe database
bytes written to the real file name until it is verified

tests.label: 02 · Proof
tests.title: Tested against a server that lies.
tests.body: Every engine feature has to pass against our own deliberately broken test server before it ships. These are the things it does on purpose:
rows: Reconnects and continues from the last byte it wrote.
Notices, falls back to a single connection, and does not corrupt the file.
Sends no file size at all
Sees the changed ETag and starts clean instead of stitching two files together.
Pauses and lets you paste a fresh link. Everything already downloaded is kept.
Retries with back-off, then carries on.
Keeps every connection busy, so the total is still as fast as the line allows.
tests.note: The test server is in the repository: internal/testsrv.

more.label: 03 · Everything else
more.title: Small app. Not a small feature list.
items: Browser extension
Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi hand downloads over with their cookies, so files behind a login work. It also finds videos on the page.
Torrents
Magnet links and .torrent files. Nothing is seeded after you finish.
Video and streams
HLS and DASH streams saved as one file, plus video sites.
FTP
For the servers that never moved on.
Queue and limits
Active-download limit, global and per-file speed caps, categories, scheduler.
16 languages
Including real right-to-left layouts for Arabic, Persian and Urdu.

privacy.label: 07 · Privacy
privacy.title: It only talks to the servers you download from.
privacy.body: No analytics, no telemetry, no account, no ads, no bundled offers. Filenames from servers are cleaned against path tricks, finished files get your system's "downloaded from the internet" mark, and the local API listens only on 127.0.0.1 behind a secret token. This website has no trackers either. Read the threat model.

faq.label: 08 · Questions
faq.title: Questions
items: Is Peregrine really free?
Yes. It is open source under GPL-3.0. There is no paid version, no trial, no ads and no bundled offers.
Is it a good alternative to IDM?

It covers what most people use IDM for: many connections per file, resuming broken downloads and catching downloads from the browser. It is free and also runs on macOS. It is an early preview, so expect rough edges and please report them.
Why does Windows SmartScreen warn me?
The builds are not code-signed yet. Click More info, then Run anyway. You can check the file against SHA256SUMS.txt and the signed build provenance on GitHub.
Does it work on Linux?
On Linux, Peregrine is a command-line tool for x64 and ARM64. The desktop app is for Windows and macOS.
Does it collect any data?
No. No analytics and no telemetry. It only connects to the internet for the downloads you start.

footer.tagline: Peregrine is named after the peregrine falcon, the fastest animal on Earth.
